tips.comment: Comfortable winner on debut for William Haggas over 1 mile at Kempton in December. It was a taking effort by the Kingman colt who quickened nicely to win there. Tom Marquand (SR 20%) booked. Opposition not very strong so the selection is expected to score on seasonal debut.

Given three of these are making their belated reappearance, Summer Heat works out at about a 6/4 chance. She did nothing wrong when finishing second to a useful-looking sort from Roger Varian's yard, and with cheekpieces applied, might have enough to take this with a fitness edge.
Showed some promise on debut when finishing 6th of 9 last September. Not seen since but should show some improvement for having had that run and holds an each way chance.

Mary Anne Maximus is a 3-year-old filly trained by Brian Ellison. She didn't show much on debut at 200-1, beaten 16.5 lengths, but dwelt at the start and was slowly away. Brian Ellison is in good form, picking up 5 wins from the last 23 starters. She is out of a pretty ordinary dam related to six winners, five of which won on the flat, notably Talwar with 4 out of 19 wins, winning three times as a 2-year-old and a listed race on 3-year-old reappearance. A speculative bet, but in receipt of up to a stone from most of her rivals, a speculative each-way bet is warranted under Faye McManoman.

The 4-year-old has run well in his three turf runs this year, going very close with good ratings posted in his last two races. Ridden by an amateur in his last two races, he now has an experienced jockey in the saddle.

Lovely big grey who, at 10 years of age, has returned to form in the last couple of runs with a win at Southwell, leading all the way, and then just getting run out of it to finish 3rd at Ripon when up in class. Could surprise again and has solid each-way chances.

The Good Biscuit was sent off second favourite last time at Ayr but ran too keen and was no match for the highly progressive Woohoo. He's on a favourable handicap mark compared to this time last year when runner-up in a class 4 off 79. He is given another chance at longer odds.

Backing Travis, the 4-year-old gelding by Advertise trained by Geoffrey Harker, in tomorrow’s 7f Weatherbys ePassport Handicap at Thirsk. He arrives in decent touch, producing a solid 4th of 9 at Redcar on 20 June (7f on good ground), showing he’s race-fit and handling the mid-summer conditions well. His recent form includes a respectable 2nd at Ayr in May along with two further minor placings. That consistency suggests the pathways towards a big run.
Rated around 61??'a shade below his peak??'Travis is now operating off a fair mark. Thirsk’s 7f sharp course, where early pace sets up a late surge, should suit his come-from-behind style. A mid-pack ride is expected before he launches his challenge in the final furlong.
Won a Class 2 (0-100) over this trip at York last time out. Raised 4 pounds as a consequence but looks the progressive type and eased in grade to Class 3 (0-90).

Two return runs for the 4-year-old this year and a big run three weeks ago, beaten just 1/2L in a 19-runner handicap. High RPR rating posted, but the run can be marked up as much better than the stats as he was easily the best runner from those drawn high.
Won at Newcastle in March. Disappointing last time out after a slow start, but now taking a drop in class and well supported in the market.

Made all victory at York and would have done it easier if not drifting left-handed in the final furlong. Jockey retained after that victory. This tighter track and high stall draw should help. Handicapper may have him in grasp though, and each-way insurance is advised.

Mythical Phoenix drifted up the handicap last season after starting off with five consecutive 2nd places, which pushed his mark from 80 to peak at 88. This season started with a reasonable performance at Doncaster over 6f, finishing 4th of 9, just weakening late on off 86. He should do better back at Thirsk.

Manila Scouse dropped a hint at Hamilton last time that he was ready to strike form. That was a strong handicap with winners already coming from it. Manila Scouse hit top form around this time last season, and with the yard firing well just now, he can go close here.

Tinto last won here last August when today's rider was last in the saddle on GF. He only missed out by a nose here in May. Although up 1 lb for that, I still think he could be worth an EW 4P with Paul again.
Veteran horse who had a day to forget LTO when 16 of 16 at Haydock back in May of this year, but now only operating 1 lb higher than last winning mark should make him a threat.

Inconsistent but talented individual who returned with a very promising 2nd at Carlisle in May. Well beaten in a class 2 at Ripon last time but that's easily forgiven so would be no surprise to see him bounce back this afternoon.

Topteam stands out as the day’s strongest bet at Thirsk. Lightly raced, improving, and partnered with top jockey Oisin Murphy, he’s well-handicapped in a modest field. With market confidence behind him and a strong trainer in A.M. Balding, this 3-year-old has the ideal setup to deliver a win.
Won on debut over 5f. Finished fourth over 5f here last time. Looks the sort who will benefit from the step up in trip. Should go well.

Promising debut in a minor event at Carlisle saw him finish a close-up 4th over 5f, but he wasn’t given a hard race and should show the benefits of that initial experience here over a slightly longer trip.

First-time starter that has been working well for some time now, makes his debut here today. Even though his stablemate has the experience, if not needing a run or two to be focused, he will be in the mix.

Straight Ahead has only had two runs to sixth, and they have both been in big money C2's, with the latest run last month being a bit further away. But I put that down to the GS going, and I think today's GF and dropping to a more realistic C5 could see a result, especially with Sam James in the saddle this time, who seems to be on a bit of a roll of late. EW.

This maiden has participated in 2 races. She showed more promise than her first outing, placing 5th in a novice event at this course and distance 15 days ago. If she continues to improve, this 2-year-old may offer an each-way profit at 20/1.

Was totally unfancied by the markets when making his racecourse debut in a maiden at Haydock over an extended 8f. There were clear signs of inexperience in the early stages of that race but shaped with promise late on without coming under too much pressure. Better still last time at Beverley when 2nd of 10 over an extended 7f trip. Back at a mile here and can go close.
Gentle Touch made a big improvement on the return from a break last month when dropping to C5 and up to 7f. There could be more to come now at 1 mile and second up.

Wolfpack jumped left-handed when leaving the stalls in a valuable novice stakes at Doncaster last time out. That was after a break of 198 days on soft ground. Down in class, he should be sharper for the run and offers a bit of value against the favourite .
Although making its debut this afternoon, with the stable still doing well over the last 14 days, it may be worth taking a chance with this debutant. It is the trainer's only runner of the day.

Dooley is a bit of a long shot as he returned from a break in a C2 at 7f way down the pack after a duff start. But he did make some headway in the last furlong, which makes me think that today's 1 mile and getting back in C5 could get a result if he gets a better start. EW
Won over C&D and was unlucky in this race last year. Did not get the best of runs last time out at Wetherby. Change of jockey might help, and with a clear run, should make amends and win again.
A big price for a horse that was unlucky last time out at Wetherby 13 days ago. Beaten a short head, it can improve here to go close.

Possibly not suited by the drop in trip when a beaten favourite over 5 furlongs at Ripon last time out. Won over the extended 5 furlongs at Wetherby in April 2024 off a mark of 61 and races 10 pounds below that today racing off 51.

A wide-open sprint handicap where 12/1 shot Gis A Sub appeals. He has dropped to a very good-looking mark and ran well last time at Newcastle, doing his best work late on. A nice high draw here looks a big plus, and he does also go well here.

The 4yo filly has gone close in all her four races this year, all over 5f, good ratings posted and plenty of winners coming out of those races. She has a good draw, she has run well over 7f previous and this 6f trip could be ideal. She was rated 11lb higher this time last year.

Korroor finished 3rd behind rival Golden Prosperity last time in a classified stakes at Nottingham. He has run in classified stakes in his last three races, winning his first at Newcastle in March. He has also been running mainly on the all-weather in the last year but is equally proficient on turf, although yet to win on it, and does not want rain.

It's all about the jockey for me here since Beasley has been 2nd and 3rd on his two rides on this horse. On each of those runs, there are collateral form lines for close-up horses, which suggests this lightly raced horse could be capable of being competitive off this mark of 53. There are several clues that the horse should easily be in the 60s ratings on the evidence of those two runs. I'd like to see the jockey use hold-up tactics for a change, which I also think would improve her chances.

Only 1-21 and yet to win a handicap or on turf, but posted some solid early season efforts off this mark before below par in Class 4 at York last time. Not one for maximum faith given his record, but worth another chance this afternoon on this drop back into Class 5.
Getting fitter and fitter with each and every run, should be at his best for this event and could show these the way home.

The 6-year-old was back on turf for her last two races, blowing the start during May but was much better four weeks ago in an 11-runner handicap, beaten 2 lengths. She sat last but finished fast in the final furlong. Something to build on and is on a handy mark going off past form.

The market leaders make limited appeal, so Mereside Madness is given a chance. He ran in a better race than this last time, in which half a dozen made the frame next time out. A drop in grade from class 4 to 5 should make him competitive in this event.

At the bottom third of the handicap mark in this field, but is a C&D winner and only 1lb higher than the last winning mark. Five months of inactivity could be an issue, but if he can overcome this, then I do fancy his chances.

Backing Electric Avenue, the 5-year-old Outstrip mare trained by Ivan Furtado, in tomorrow’s 7f Class 5 handicap at Thirsk. She arrives in sharp nick after landing a confidence-boosting win at Redcar on 27 May, tracking into the race before taking control inside the final furlong??'showing she handles a strong gallop and stays the trip well. In between, she ran 6th at Thirsk on 17 May, closing from the rear in a modest field and proving she stays on the rising track.
Rated around 64, she looks nicely handicapped off her current mark. That Redcar triumph demonstrates she's race-fit, progressive off a break, and ticks the boxes for this Thirsk assignment. Expect her to break cleanly, settle midfield behind a solid early pace, and produce a strong late surge up the straight.

The model I run suggests Woodland Adventure can win this one. Woodland Adventure lines up here with the highest RPR of this 10-horse race and doesn't look penalized for it in the weights. Jockey claims further lbs and looks to make it 3 wins on the spin with some impressive form shown so far. Woodland Adventure is already the short odds-on favorite. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This result has been largely driven by the poor value with the short odds on offer.

Arayapearl ran a really promising race first time out when 3rd in a contest that is beginning to work out well and the horse that finished a well beaten 7th in that race ran a very good third yesterday at Stratford, finishing ahead of Jury Belle which on a line with Woodland Adventure gives her the clear beating of the odds on favourite. The Bowens are a force to be reckoned with in bumpers and this one has a nice pedigree to go along with it.

BELIEVEINTHEMOON comes from a yard who have enjoyed a decent start to 2025 and who go under the radar with what they have. This mare has an each-way shout based on her rules debut at this venue and a relatively quick turnaround reads well for her chance.
Not beaten far when runner-up over an extended two miles here last month. Shaped as though he would appreciate this step up in trip.

She Has Notions has not won since around this time last year but has spent this year's three runs since the break hurdling. Not great with two PU, but those runs were up around 3 miles. I think the return to 2m4f today, a trip he last won at here with Sean Bowen in the saddle in this last year, bodes well for today.

The Evan Williams trained syndicate owned Henry Box Brown ticks a lot of the boxes, he is a c&d winner and acts on the ground. He is fit and well, Ellis Collier takes off 5lbs and a big run is anticipated.

Catboy, a winner over hurdles at Fontwell, made a fair start over fences on chase debut last time (2m4f good Uttox). That was his second run back following a break. He travelled well for a long way and was not pushed once beaten. He would have learned plenty and be sharper today. It was a stronger race than he faces today, and with just a touch of improvement, he looks capable enough to make the frame at least against today's rivals. With a 4-place payout, he offers EW value.

Zacony Rebel was rated as high as 129 over fences just two years ago in 2023. Although having shown very little form recently, that has been over hurdles, and he could still have some ability in chases above his current mark of 95. His last chase was way back in October 2023 when rated 124.

Hammer Dan won at Newton Abbot and Stratford last season and returned from 11 months off when second back at Newton Abbot in a handicap last month. He is up 3 lbs higher here and looks the most likely winner.

Consistent sort, this one is coming back after a short break, so should be refreshed. Trying this trip for the first time, but the stable is in good form, so I think a frame finish is almost certain at least.
The step up in trip could just be what this consistent mare needs. The stable struck with their only runner yesterday and could do so again today.
Rounding into form, or so it seems to be. But when he's in that mood, he could be a very dangerous customer in this event.

After his success at Stratford at the end of May, his record over fences stands at 7-9. A 4lb increase shouldn't impede another strong showing, particularly with Bowen, who has an exceptional 28% win rate, aboard.
Won at the first time of asking over fences last time. The 3lb rise for that win looks fair and with further improvement, this one should be able to go in again.

The model I run suggests Fame And Fun can win this one. Fame And Fun lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 8 runner field but has the lowest official ranking. This means Fame And Fun steps out carrying the lowest amount of weight and by quite an amount. Most other horses carry at least 1 stone more over this 2m 7f trip. Good third when last out 13 days ago and Sean Bowen, champion jockey, picks up the reins. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Halondo took a step forward to a close second on chase debut in May after running out of steam. He may benefit from the drop to 2m7f and getting Harry in the saddle for this one.
Drops in grade here, the first time for almost 2 years down in a 0-120. His mark of 121 is 2 lb lower than when winning over course and distance less than a year ago. Each way chance.

Chemical Warfare has a good strike rate of wins as a chaser - 8 from 17. Excuses for the last 2 runs with 3m5f stretching his limits and a run over hurdles that isn't his strong point. Dropped 2lb and this trip should suit. He already has 1 win from 1 chase start here.
Decent point to point & bumper form should transfer to hurdles pretty well. Has a good chance of coming out on top here
His first two starts of the season figure well. Now that he's better off for those efforts, he could run away with it all here.

The model I run suggests Currumbin can win this one. This result has been driven by Currumbin having the joint highest RPR in this smaller 5-horse race. Prior course and distance winner and looks to repeat that here. Last win came only 7 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. Wheeled out in quick succession here. Early market looks like it's an open race. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This has been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

Won well last time, pulling clear with the runner-up in a well-run race. Moves up 6 lb here on just his 3rd handicap start over hurdles, but considering his flat mark was in the mid to high 80s, his mark here of 96 should be well within his range over jumps.
Goes well here and just got collared close to home a couple of weeks ago by a progressive horse. Anything similar and must go close.

PLAY PRETEND has previously been well supported in Listed company. He takes in his second run back from his break here and is still just a four year old with scope through the handicap sphere. He gets to race from a now career-low mark and should be dangerous in ths low level handicap company.

Made a strange stable debut last time out when well beaten. I am sure this one is better than that, and coming from this top trainer, I'm sure it will improve this afternoon. A frame finish is possible.

The model I run suggests Cawthorne Banker can win this one. Cawthorne Banker lines up here with an RPR that is way ahead of the others in this race and has an official ranking that is third last. This subsequently means Cawthorne Banker goes out carrying the third lowest amount of weight around this 2m round trip. Current top of the market carries well over a stone more in weight. Prior distance winner but has not shown any signs of form for a while now. Richie McLernon picks up the reins, who's a trusted pair of hands, and the visor is tried for the first time to try and spark a bit of revival. The model has issued a 'very high' stake indicator, which translates to a 4pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This result has been driven by the very high value on offer at 26s.

City of Ruins has just 6 starts in his career, often having one or two runs, then having a break in between. So, he may be a bit of a fragile type. Well-bred, his pedigree wouldn't look out of place on the flat. He has had issues with his jumping, but despite his few runs and jumping errors, he has been placed a few times and shown he can go well fresh. So, given his big price, he looks worth a little each way.

Gone In Sixty arrives in good form, having followed a reappearance 3rd place with a 14 lengths win over this distance at Fakenham. Today's claimer rode that day, and in this race, that will stand as an advantage. Noble Recall also won last time under today's jockey and might prove EW and RFC material.

Has massively improved for his new trainer, being placed in all three of his races for him, having previously run deplorably in this country. Now runs off 89. He won on the flat in France a couple of years ago off 80, so this jumps mark should be well within his grasp.

Gms Prince put in one of his best races when upped to 2m4f at Market Rasen, 2m4f good to soft in February. Has since run four times over shorter trips. Fell in one and was staying on well in 2 of the other 3, while not settling on his latest run. Has shown he acts on quicker ground and now runs off a career-low mark back up to 2m4f. This race lacks some strength in depth and he has solid EW claims at 18/1.

Not the best start to the month yesterday, and DARCY'S GLANCE could go the same way, to be honest. But she's back up to two and a half miles, and today's jockey, Shane Quinlan, got her close in April with a decent run for a long way from 5 lbs higher in the weights. At this price, considered each-way.

ZARHANYA is double-entered at this track across the next week and both entries are over this trip. She is a fascinating low-mileage later-starting mare who comes from a shrewd yard and these overnight odds appear to underestimate her chance in this low grade handicap hurdle.
Comes here on the back of a win last time out. The 5 lbs rise isn't overly harsh considering this one's progressive nature. Should go close.

Savannah Smiles was 4th and beaten less than 2 lengths 2 runs back over 6f here at Chepstow. Now over 5f, where she has been 2nd here before, I expect a good run, especially with Elizabeth Gale taking 5lb off.
Chepstow is not every horse's cup of tea, but Outer Edge likes it, having won here last August. The trainer and jockey are in good form, and Outer Edge likes good/firm ground as it is at his level.
Still without a win in her 5 races but seems to be heading in the right direction. Good run at Yarmouth 3 weeks ago, 3/8, and could progress from there today.

Some Nightmare is in stall 8 with a mark of 62, which looks about right based on recent runs. He won here three starts back off 55 despite being slowly away. He likes this track but has failed to back that up since, including a 6-length sixth last time off 56. Trainer John O'Shea is a regular winner at this course, and jockey Taryn Langley claims 5lb, which helps. He has a strong course record with 5 wins from 17 runs and is usually held up off the pace, which suits stall 8 and the possible good tempo here. He wears cheekpieces again, which have helped him in the past. With solid course form and a setup that suits him, he has an outside each-way shout if bouncing back to his best today.
Has only won once but has been running well of late, placing in all of the last 4 starts, finishing 2nd on 3 occasions. Should be there or thereabouts.

Only having a third run on turf, did run well at Bath last time out, and if building on that run, could well add to the Newcastle win. And for a six-year-old, might have room to improve, having only run six times to date.

Three underwhelming starts for Charlie Johnston before moving to Tony Carroll. Has had two starts for new connections, both over 6f and both with 7lb claimer Matthew Lloyd Slater on board. Has shown speed and shown better form, looking as though a try at the minimum 5f is well worth a go. This is bottom drawer handicapping, and off a lowly mark of 42 (on account of 7lb), she could well make her mark tell.

Backing Glamorous Jewel, the lightly raced 3-year-old Ardad filly trained by Christopher Mason, in tonight’s Bath Racecourse Thanks NetBet Classified Stakes over 5f 16y at Chepstow. While she only managed a fifth of eight last time out on 21 May, that performance has since been frankly boosted??'Art Of Fox, who finished just ahead of her that day, followed up with a win on his next outing, confirming the strength of the form.
Despite the modest final placing, Glamorous Jewel showed pace and was only beaten around seven lengths??'an effort that looks much more creditable now. Rated around 46 and stepping back down in class, she’s stoutly held and ready to capitalise with the confidence from that outing. With a small field of 10 runners, a good draw, and the form line now strengthened, she presents strong each-way value at likely odds of 30/1??'40/1.
Flying Comet should improve for his first run at Nottingham over 5f, where he finished 3rd after his slow start. After recovering, he faded late on there.

Shams looks in a good position to win this if getting out fast and has the progeny to do so. Joe Levey has an 18% strike rate at Chepstow this season, as does the trainer, and a big run is expected. Distance suits perfectly. E/W prospect.
The step up to 2m could be the making of Casual Encounter after running respectably over 12f the last twice. Being a 3yo, she looks to have plenty of improvement.

Nearest at the finish over this trip at Catterick under today's jockey when 3rd of 7, beaten by 1.25 lengths off this mark on penultimate start. Will welcome the extra 2 furlongs after racing over a mile and three quarters at Chelmsford last time out.

A low-grade 2m handicap. The 4yo can be a little hit or miss, but he does have three career wins. He’s fine with the fast ground, down to an attractive mark. He’s running in a very weak handicap, and the good apprentice claiming 7lb can only improve his chances.

Having gone 29 races without a win in 2023, this 10-year-old is in need of a turnaround. He finished 6th in a handicap at Bath 18 days ago. A major rebound is required, but the jockey's 7lb claim should help ease the pressure, making the veteran a promising each-way choice at 33/1.
Showed plenty of improvement when entering handicap company and winning at Bath last month. Up 4 lb, but that's likely to be manageable, and no surprise to see following up.
Kept on inside the final furlong when 3rd of 14 over this trip at Windsor in an apprentice race 9 days ago. The winner, Lequinto, has won twice again since to boost the form.

This looks easier for GOGO YUBARI, who is thrown in on the basis of his last turf run, which was a close run thing from three pounds higher. Could land this if running to that form against lesser opposition. Saver on Sun Keeper, who could run well from a deep price.

Hopefully SUN KEEPER has put the temperamental streak behind her and it was a bit more like last time out when beaten by a couple of lengths at Doncaster. Two lbs lower now and the six furlong trip shouldn't be a problem either. Considered if continuing to progress.

Raced as if something was amiss when beaten 15 lengths over 6 furlongs at Windsor last time out when well supported in the market. Wears the first-time tongue-tie, which could explain the previous performance. If that has the desired effect, he could go well with the drop in trip aiding that appeal.

Won only her second run at Doncaster last summer but really struggled last time out in handicap debut when 14 of 14 at Windsor last month. At least the tricky starting mark has been eased, but she has to make improvements to have a chance tomorrow.

Four career runs for the 3-year-old and three solid runs in defeat. He was a good 4th of 12 on his handicap debut three weeks ago, but he met an endless amount of traffic problems from 3 furlongs out. Same mark for this contest and worth another chance.

Made a winning debut for new yard over this trip at Goodwood last month and with further improvement expected to come from that run following a 212 day break, she should go well again here being a former course winner over a mile and a quarter.

Graham has spent most of this year hurdling. When last on the flat last year, he returned from a break and was pants but was placed when second up off a 78. With a return from a short break last month at the back of the pack, I would expect more improvement today and worth an EW while on a 75 today.

Diamondonthehill has done well without winning for most runs since a short break in December, with all but the latest run being on the AW. However, he did grab a win in April and in May returned to turf with a decent second. He should be able to build on that, as his last turf win was in a C3 off today's mark last year.

Aurora Majesty has ability and is well capable of being involved in the placings if getting out fast. The trainer shows a 16% strike rate at Epsom, and top jockey Hollie Doyle works well together. E/W possibilities.

Mafnood started slowly last time at Goodwood but was only beaten 2L. He hasn't won for a long time, but this race is a chance for him to get back to winning ways. Jockey Jim Crowley knows him well and was the last one to win on him, and it's his only ride of the day.
Third at 28-1 on last two outings. Goes well at Epsom and two of last three wins have come over course and distance. Return to seven furlongs at Epsom in his favour. Makes fair appeal at odds of 6-1.

DREAM OF MISCHIEF returns to last winning mark, and has decent course form here at Epsom so could well put the two disappointing runs at Goodwood and Ascot behind him now returning to a preferred track. Grade and Going all look good and he just looks very difficult to rule out.

The stable tends to be good with the sprinters, so I'd take note when they've got one in the mood. ALAZHIR looks to fit the bill here. The jockey cancels out the rise for the last win, and there's no reason he can't win again. I'd be surprised if he goes off at this price; it should be shorter.

I'm not convinced the market leaders here are the ones to be on. Far Above Dream won his first race for James Owen and was then entered in a 64k Class 2 handicap, which was a step too far. Obviously improved and looks capable of winning this.

Demonstrating impressive performance under this apprentice, he achieved a remarkable victory in a 6-runner handicap at Leicester just 18 days ago, showcasing his ability to run the race effectively. Although he's up 3lb, it's evident that he is in outstanding form.
Annexation was a close 2nd at Doncaster last time and was well clear of the rest, he should be well up to winning this Apprentice Handicap with Jack Doughty in the saddle.

The 4yo filly has gone close in all her four races this year, all over 5f, good ratings posted and plenty of winners coming out of those races. She has a good draw, she has run well over 7f previous and this 6f trip could be ideal. She was rated 11lb higher this time last year.

Made a positive impression by coming in 2nd out of 5 in a novice race at Newmarket 12 days ago, though was no match for the winner. Establishing a strong standard and looks a formidable contender, particularly with both the jockey and trainer in excellent form.

Karen Jewell and Robert Havlin combine here to try and get Pablo Prince home at good odds. No world-beater by any stretch of the imagination, but can be useful on his day and has placed twice when produced second-up previously. Needs to find a bit extra off the back of that resuming 9th and may need another yet to peak, but Havlin knows the horse well (two of the horse's four wins have come with him in the saddle) and PP has won three of his four raceday wins at this trip. So, at the odds, might represent an each-way chance.
Kansas has finished placed in all three of his runs so far and was two places ahead of main rival Baker Blue last time and looks the most likely winner.

Baker Blue has come up against some good level opposition and performed well on all 3 starts. Has 3 lengths to find on the short-price favorite here, but that was after an awkward break out of the stalls. Could be closer matched for this contest and represents the value bet for the race, in my opinion.

Looked in need of the experience on his debut at Down Royal. Bearing that in mind, and the troubled passage he endured during the race, he didn’t fare too badly. Should be more to come and worth a second look.

Namiid shaped with strong promise on debut at Navan, finishing sixth behind Kansas in a race that's proving a key formline. He travelled well for much of the race and was only caught late, showing enough tactical speed and stamina for today's 5f. Trainer JP Murtagh is doing well with 2YOs this season, and draw 4 suits on a track favouring pace.

SPICETOWN showed good pace on his debut and is a juvenile colt who attracted a little support first-up. Likely that tells us he is considered a forward type and Tipperary's sharp circuit over this minimum trip could see him to good effect with a talented 7lb claimer called up.

Sir Yoshi is well clear on ratings and has his going at Tipperary but he has only won once in May 2024 as a two year old over course and distance. He has however run respectably at Listed level in his last three runs.

Had been off the track for 6 months when making a satisfactory return at Cork over 5f at the beginning of April, finishing a close-up 3rd. Shaped as though the run was just needed then but ran no sort of race back there next time when last of 12 over a slightly longer trip, albeit in a tougher race. Made his handicap debut over 5f again at Cork last time but was only 7th of 8, albeit not beaten that far. This looks a tough race and probably playing for minor honours.
Spring Is Here may come out on top back on a better surface to get her first win after a disappointing run here on softer going when only just finishing ahead of Gelato.

This looks quite weak for a Listed contest. Back from Royal Ascot, First Approach may be the answer. Aidan O'Brien trained No Nay Never colt out of a speedy mare. Won maiden over five furlongs on second start. Ran in a strong Group 3 at the Curragh prior to Royal Ascot, so this is easier. Cheekpieces applied and can progress in this company.
Might be the value here, although some eight pounds worse off with the favorite, Spring Is Here has plenty of room to improve on that run and is not easy to ignore.

The 3-year-old appears formidable after finishing a commendable 2nd in a handicap at Fairyhouse just 34 days ago. Looking better positioned than most competitors, she stands a good chance of excelling once more while representing the thriving O'Leary stable.

Been improving with each outing this year and was a running on 3rd of 13 three starts ago at the Curragh despite being unsuited by the drop back to 6f. Ran to a similar level next time at Fairyhouse when 5th back at 7f before running to a similar level last time at Limerick kept to 7f. Goes up slightly in trip here from a falling mark and looks interesting.

Beautiful Affair has placed twice at Dundalk over this distance and has ability if getting a clear run. Joseph O'Brien shows a 14% strike rate this season at Tipperary, and a top jockey booking is encouraging. E/W ability.

Whilst Ross O'Sullivan's 4-year-old filly ALTIMARA hasn't quite put things together on turf (although it's very early days), her runs at Dundalk over this trip during the winter caught my eye. First, there was a strong effort in October, finishing just ½ length off in third, with both the second and fourth going on to win next time out. Two weeks later, she backed that up with a solid second, just ¾ length behind another decent sort who also won again.
Now I know what you're thinking - yes, that was the all-weather, not turf - but a return to a sharp, left-handed track over this trip might be just what this daughter of STARSPANGLEDBANNER needs. The application of first-time headgear could also sharpen her up. The trainer isn't exactly red hot but is ticking along nicely, boasting a 29.03% place strike rate in the past month. Notably, when teaming up with jockey Donagh O'Connor over the past year, the pair have returned a 30.43% place strike rate. At 16/1, there’s enough in the profile to have a small each-way nibble and scratch the itch. She may well surprise a few if rediscovering that Dundalk form.

He didn't run great at Gowran, but it was after a short break, and I think he needed the longer time to recover. He looks back to fitness now, and the trainer doesn't waste runs at this level. He tends to target low-grade prizes with improving 3YOs. The draw and going also suit his run today.
In what looks like being a wide-open race, I can see Onemoredance being the one to beat, who has won or placed in the last 3 races, including a course and distance win here at Tipperary.

Consistent improver - back-to-back strong handicap efforts at this class and mark. Well treated off 65, her mark is unchanged despite strong form, offering good odds off this. The trip is ideal for her. The step up from 1m to 1m1f looks the logical move given how strong she finishes.
Good each way bet here and could go one better. Fast Finisher, this horse, and a good price at 16/1. Stake 0.5 each way.
Can improve on last run when 2nd in a better race. Trip and going in its favor. From top stable, gets a good draw, can go close.

WONDERFULWONDERFUL is a curiously big price for a filly who appears feasibly treated ahead of her handicap debut. Her qualifying efforts suggest this trip should suit and she should step forward on the back of her recent reappearance effort. Each-way shout.

Pretty weak handicap. Crypto Crash ran fourth of sixteen over 1 mile at Leopardstown on last start (the second from that race won here yesterday). A maiden after nine outings but running off a more realistic mark. David Marnane (SR 17%) trained. Shows potential and looks well handicapped against some jaded looking handicappers.
Came back after a four months break to finish third at Leopardstown last time out. Sure to improve for that run.

Pink Socks has an excuse for the last run when the saddle slipped. The handicap mark is tumbling, and this horse has the capability to run a big race, having been runner-up on 6 occasions. This is a weak contest, and with Nicola Burns in great form, her 7lb claim can make a big difference.

ROCHESTER MIKE had a valid reason for his poor showing latest. He is third-up with potential to peak for this spell and he has fallen a long way down the ratings since first starting out in handicap company. Now a five year old having matured with promise on his penultimate start he appeals.
